dependencies.title: System Dependencies
dependencies.autoInstallTitle: Install required system dependencies from Terminal
dependencies.autoInstallOpened: Terminal opened. Xcode Command Line Tools, Homebrew, MacFUSE, ntfs-3g, and fswatch will install automatically. You only need to handle passwords and system dialogs.
dependencies.installGuideIntro: To install or reinstall dependencies, please follow the instructions below to install manually in the terminal:
dependencies.missingDepsDetected: Missing dependencies detected, please see installation guide below

fsKit.name: FSKit (Native File System Framework)
fsKit.description: Apple's file system extension framework (macOS 15.4+). Once the Nigate FSKit extension is installed and enabled, choose FSKit in Settings > Mount Backend to mount NTFS natively.
fsKit.installGuide:
1. Build and install Nigate.app via macos/Scripts/build.sh (extension lives under Contents/PlugIns).
2. Open System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions → File System Extensions and enable Nigate NTFS.
3. Switch Mount Backend to FSKit in the app Settings.
If the control plane is not ready, explicitly select ntfs-3g (Compatibility). Mount paths never silently fall back.

swift.name: Xcode Command Line Tools
swift.description: Apple official development tools, providing Swift compiler and basic development libraries
swift.installGuide: Run the above command in the terminal, an installation window will pop up, follow the prompts to complete the installation. The installation process may take several minutes to tens of minutes, please wait patiently.

brew.name: Homebrew
brew.description: Package manager for macOS, used to install and manage software packages
brew.installGuide: Run the above command in the terminal and follow the prompts to complete the installation. If the network is slow, try the China mainland mirror command below.

macfuse.name: MacFUSE
macfuse.description: File system user space framework, required by ntfs-3g.
macfuse.installGuide: If macOS shows a system approval prompt for MacFUSE or its file system extension, verify the developer and extension name and approve only if you confirmed that you installed the official package. Follow the current system prompts; only change Gatekeeper temporarily as described in the macOS upgrade steps below, and restore it afterward.
macfuse.appleSiliconSecurity: If an Apple silicon Mac asks to approve a third-party kernel extension, follow Apple's official steps: shut down, press and hold the power button to open startup options, choose Options to enter Recovery, then open Startup Security Utility. Select Reduced Security for the system disk and enable “Allow user management of kernel extensions from identified developers.” This lowers startup security; do so only if the system requires it and you have confirmed the official MacFUSE package.
macfuse.upgradeError: After a macOS upgrade, if you see “The installed version of macFUSE is too old for the operating system,” follow these steps.
macfuse.upgradeSecurityNotice: The command below disables Gatekeeper system-wide and enables the “Anywhere” option, reducing system security. Run it only temporarily to upgrade the official MacFUSE package; re-enable Gatekeeper immediately after installation and extension approval.
macfuse.upgradeCommandIntro: After enabling it, run this command in Terminal to upgrade MacFUSE:
macfuse.upgradeApproval: After upgrading, if macOS says the extension was blocked, allow the MacFUSE extension from the verified developer in System Settings > Privacy & Security, then restart if prompted. If it still will not load on Apple silicon, review the startup security policy described above. After approving the extension and completing any required restart, run the command below immediately to re-enable Gatekeeper.

ntfs3g.name: ntfs-3g
ntfs3g.description: NTFS file system driver, providing NTFS read-write support
ntfs3g.installGuide: Homebrew and MacFUSE must be installed first. Run the above command in the terminal to install.
ntfs3g.installGuideTip: After installing macFUSE and ntfs-3g, go to System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions → Extensions → By Category → File System Extensions. Then click the info icon and enable ntfs-3g (if present) and macFUSE.

fswatch.name: fswatch (Optional)
fswatch.description: File system event monitoring tool for zero-latency device detection (event-driven mode)
fswatch.installGuide: fswatch is an optional performance optimization tool. After installation, it enables zero-latency device detection and reduces CPU usage by 90%+. Run the above command to install.

macosVersion.installGuide: If your macOS version is too low, please upgrade your system through System Settings > Software Update. This tool requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or higher to run properly.

devices.title: NTFS Devices
devices.emptyHint: Please insert an NTFS formatted removable storage device
devices.resetTooltip: Reset device (unmount and fix, for resolving Resource busy errors)
devices.repairConfirmNote: ntfsfix can only handle basic issues and cannot replace Windows chkdsk. Repairing may cause data loss.
devices.renameNote:
Note:
1. Do not rename while files are transferring — it can interrupt the copy or corrupt the volume label
2. After you confirm, the new name is written, then the volume is unmounted and remounted so it takes effect
devices.formatConfirm: This will erase all partitions and data on the entire disk!
devices.formatConfirmNote:
1. This cannot be undone. Back up important data first.
2. Formatting may take a while and will unmount and remount the volume several times.
3. Do not disconnect the device or interrupt the process. Please wait until it finishes.
Continue?
devices.mountConfirm: Are you sure you want to mount {name} as read-write mode?
devices.mountConfirmNote:
Note:
• This requires administrator privileges, and the system will prompt for a password
• If this NTFS device was previously used on a Windows computer with Fast Startup enabled, you may need to plug it back into the Windows computer and fully shut down before trying
devices.unmountConfirm: Are you sure you want to unmount {name}?
devices.ejectConfirm: Are you sure you want to eject {name}?
devices.ejectConfirmNote:
Note:
• After ejecting, the device will be completely disconnected from the system
• The device will be removed from the list and needs to be reinserted to use
• Please ensure no programs are using the device

icons.title: Interface Icons Guide
icons.intro: The application's main interface provides several functional icons to help you quickly access common features:

autoMount.name: Auto Read-Write Icon
autoMount.description: When enabled, the background mounts newly inserted read-only NTFS volumes as read-write, whether or not a window is open. A volume you restore to read-only stays unchanged for the current connection. The icon appears blue when active.

trayMode.name: Tray Mode Icon
trayMode.description: When enabled, closing the window will minimize the application to the system tray instead of quitting. The icon appears purple when active.

preventSleep.name: Prevent Sleep Icon
preventSleep.description: Off by default. Click to cycle: Off → Prevent Sleep (coffee brown, always on) → Smart Prevent Sleep (teal) → Off. Status protection locks this button.

protect.name: Status Protection Icon
protect.description: Long press for 3 seconds to toggle protection status. When protected, auto read-write, tray mode, and the prevent-sleep icon are locked to prevent accidental operations. The icon appears green with a pulse animation when protected.

about.name: About Icon
about.description: Opens the about window to view application information and project links.

preventSleepModes.title: Prevent Sleep Modes
preventSleepModes.intro: The title bar coffee icon is off by default. Click to cycle Off → Prevent Sleep → Smart Prevent Sleep → Off. Status protection locks this button.
preventSleepModes.off: Off: Sleep is not blocked. The icon is uncolored.
preventSleepModes.always: Prevent Sleep (coffee brown): Sleep stays blocked even when idle. Enter this mode only from the title bar icon; the Settings checkbox does not control it.
preventSleepModes.smart: Smart Prevent Sleep (teal): Watches currently mounted NTFS volumes only. Sleep is blocked while those volumes have read/write traffic, then allowed again about 20 seconds after traffic stops. With no mounted NTFS volume, or while idle, the Mac is not kept awake. The Settings checkbox syncs only with this mode.
preventSleepModes.quit: Sleep prevention stops when you quit the app.

refresh.name: Refresh Icon
refresh.description: Refreshes the device list and re-detects connected NTFS devices.

done.name: Done Icon
done.description: After format or repair succeeds, the corresponding format/repair icon briefly changes to this completion mark, then returns after about 3 seconds.

settings.title: Application Settings
settings.savePasswordDesc: When enabled, the app will securely save your administrator password using macOS Keychain for automatic input
settings.deletePasswordConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete the saved password?
settings.deletePasswordError: Failed to delete password, please try again
settings.startupTabDesc: Select the default tab to display when the app starts
settings.autoMountDesc: When enabled, the background mounts newly inserted read-only NTFS volumes as read-write without opening a window. A volume restored to read-only stays unchanged for the current connection
settings.mountBackendDesc: FSKit needs macOS 15.4+ with the Nigate FSKit extension installed and enabled. Once ready, select FSKit to mount natively.
settings.mountBackendUnavailableDesc: The FSKit control plane is not ready yet (enabling a system extension is not enough). Install/enable the Nigate FSKit extension, or explicitly choose ntfs-3g compatibility.
settings.trayModeDesc: When enabled, closing the window will minimize to the system tray instead of quitting the app. You can quickly manage NTFS devices through the tray icon.
settings.preventSleepDesc: Watches mounted NTFS volumes only: sleep is blocked during transfers and allowed again about 20 seconds after idle. This checkbox turns on smart mode and matches the teal title-bar state; always-on (coffee brown) is title-bar only.
settings.autoStartDesc: When enabled, the app will automatically launch when the system starts
